problem:
Title: Approximation to Reciprocal times Derivative of Gamma Function

Let $\Gamma$ denote the [[Definition:Gamma Function|gamma function]].

For all $z \in \C$ such that $\cmod {\map \arg z} < \pi - \epsilon, \cmod z > 1$:

:$\dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} z} {\map \Gamma z} = \ln z + \map {\OO_\epsilon} {z^{-1} }$

where:
:$\map \OO {z^{-1} }$ denotes [[Definition:Big-O Notation|big-$\OO$ notation]]
:the [[Definition:Implied Constant|implied constant]] depends on $\epsilon$.
proof_numbered:
0001 | From [[Logarithmic Approximation of Error Term of Stirling's Formula for Gamma Function]]:
0002 | 
0003 | :$\ln \map \Gamma z = \paren {z - \dfrac 1 2} \ln z - z + \dfrac {\ln 2 \pi} 2 + \map \OO {z^{-1} }$
0004 | 
0005 | Taking the [[Definition:Derivative|derivative]] {{WRT|Differentiation}} $z$:
0006 | 
0007 | :$(1): \quad \dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} z} {\map \Gamma z} = \ln z - \dfrac 1 {2 z} + \dfrac \d {\d z} \map \OO {z^{-1} }$
0008 | 
0009 | Since there exists $\map c \epsilon > 0$ such that:
0010 | 
0011 | :$\forall \size z > 1: -\dfrac c {\size {z^{-1} } } < \size {\map \OO {z^{-1} } } < \dfrac c {\size {z^{-1} } }$
0012 | 
0013 | it follows directly that the third term in $(1)$ is $\map \OO {z^{-1} }$.
0014 | 
0015 | {{qed}}
